chunks: There is no harm in proposing in secret to (any of) these women, or keeping the intention to yourself: God is aware that you will keep them in mind. Yet do not make a promise in secret, unless you speak in a manner that is proper; and do not resolve upon marriage till the fixed term of waiting is over. Remember that God knows what is in your hearts; so be fearful of Him, and remember that God is forgiving and forbearing.

key_terms.عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ: The knot of marriage / Firm contract

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a hint in courtship and a firm marriage contract in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in Surah Al-Baqarah, establishes the etiquette of courtship by distinguishing between permissible indirect proposals and binding contracts, specifically prohibiting the finalization of marriage (‘azm al-‘iqd) before the expiration of the waiting period (iddah). Shia scholars emphasize the phrase 'what you hint at or conceal in yourselves' to validate both verbal expressions and silent intentions as valid forms of proposal, while cautioning against premature commitment to avoid emotional entanglement. The verse concludes by highlighting God’s omniscience of inner states, encouraging believers to maintain sincerity and avoid deceit in their marital pursuits.
